extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards executives, NIST staff, agency CIOs and OMB A-119 compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Governance, membership, administrative procedures, meeting and reporting requirements for the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy and related agency reporting under OMB Circular A-119. Also documents agency-level participation/use of voluntary consensus standards versus government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee membership (list of agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following agencies constitute the membership of the Committee: Department of Agriculture; Department of Defense; Department of Education; Department of Energy; Department of Health and Human Services; Department of Housing and Urban Development; Department of the Interior; Department of Justice; Department of Labor; Department of State; Department of Transportation; Department of the Treasury; Department of Veterans Affairs; Office of Consumer Affairs; Consumer Product Safety Commission; Environmental Protection Agency; Federal Communications Commission; Federal Emergency Management Agency; Federal Trade Commission; General Services Administration; International Trade Commission; Office of Management and Budget; National Aeronautics and Space Administration; National Archives and Records Administration; National Communications Systems (Dept. of Defense) (non-voting member); National Science Foundation; Nuclear Regulatory Commission; U.S. Agency for International Development; U.S. Government Printing Office (legislative liaison - non-voting member); U.S. Postal Service; Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head of each member agency shall ensure representation by a responsible high level policy official (Senior Executive Service or higher) who serves as the agency representative on the Committee and also serves as the 'Standards Executive'. Appointments to the Committee shall be for an indefinite term. Agency representatives may designate alternates of equivalent senior status to serve in their absence. Experts from organizations within the member agency may be designated by agency representatives to serve on task groups established by the Committee. Other Federal agencies may become members upon application to or invitation by the Secretary of Commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) or the Director's designee shall chair the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST shall provide administrative arrangements for the Committee including secretarial services, calling of meetings, arranging for a meeting place, and preparation of an agenda, discussion material, and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting frequency and meeting calls
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall meet at least three times each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other meetings may be called at the discretion of the Chair or at the written request of five (5) members of the Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and staffing of task groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee may establish task groups as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts from organizations within the member agency may be designated by agency representatives to serve on task groups established by the Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and internal decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance at Committee meetings by at least one half of the designated members of the Committee shall constitute a quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions internal to the Committee's operations (e.g., formation of a task group) shall be made by a majority of those present and voting. Voting on Committee business and proposals shall be limited to designated agency members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting threshold for recommendations to Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions concerning Committee recommendations to the Secretary of Commerce on governmental policy or other specified matters shall require ratification by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissenting positions on the decision may be made a matter of record. The Chair shall not vote except in the case of a tie vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting requirement (Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall submit an annual report to the Secretary of Commerce so that the Secretary may satisfy the reporting requirements set forth in OMB Circular No. A-119, as applicable to the Secretary, and in P.L. 104-113, as applicable to the head of each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each such report shall summarize the Committee's activity during the period covered and shall include a listing of all recommendations formulated by the Committee during that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter duration review
rubrics_metrics.description: The need and mission of the Committee shall be reexamined three years after the date of this Charter to determine the need for the Committee's continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination date and determination of continuation are required elements of the Charter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency annual report contents under OMB Circular A-119
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare agency reports for NIST under Circular A-119, agencies should provide accounts of A-119 activities including: the number of agency employees engaged in at least one standards-developing group; the resulting number of voluntary standards adopted since the previous year; and the number of government-unique standards adopted during the fiscal year, together with an explanation of why such a standard was chosen in lieu of a voluntary consensus standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA's method: the CIO requested accounts of A-119 activities from Agency Heads and, where necessary, placed telephone calls to selected agency members to determine if information had changed. Reports should include counts and explanations/justifications for government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for voluntary consensus standards; justification for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are expected to use voluntary consensus standards where appropriate; government-unique specifications may be used when voluntary consensus standards do not meet specific program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (AMS): AMS uses numerous voluntary consensus standards (ANSI, ASTM, Codex, IMPS, etc.) for certification and testing. AMS uses government-unique specifications for purchases (e.g., School Lunch Program) when voluntary-consensus standards do not meet the nutritional or program requirements. Agencies that develop government-unique standards should explain why a voluntary consensus standard was not suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting standards participation and adoption status
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should document participation in voluntary standards bodies, the roles of agency personnel in those bodies, and whether standards developed with agency participation have replaced or been adopted in lieu of existing agency practice standards or specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: NRCS participation in GIS Consortium, Federal Geographic Data Committee, ASTM and ASAE; ERS participation in standards and advisory teams (e.g., NAICS, CTIC, CRIS enhancement); reports should note if voluntary standards have become de facto industry standards or if agency practices are moving toward adoption, and future reports must address adoption status.
